q: In the left-child right-sibling representation of an N-ary tree, what does each node's two pointers point to?
options: Its first child and its next sibling
Its left child and its right child
Its parent and its first child
explain: Any N-ary tree becomes a binary tree this way. Following 'first child' goes down, and following 'next sibling' goes across.

q: A suffix tree of a text T of length n is built. How long does it take to check whether a pattern P of length m occurs in T?
explain: Every substring of T is a prefix of some suffix, so you just walk P down from the root, one character at a time. The text length no longer matters.

q: Why is a unique end marker such as $ appended to the text before building its suffix tree?
options: So that no suffix is a prefix of another, and every suffix ends at its own leaf
To make the text length even
To mark where the pattern starts
Because suffix trees need a binary alphabet
explain: In 'banana', the suffix 'a' is a prefix of 'ana', so it would end in the middle of an edge. With 'a$' and 'ana$', each suffix ends at a distinct leaf.

q: How many leaves does the suffix tree of a text with n characters (plus the end marker $) have?
explain: Each suffix, including the one-character suffix '$', ends at its own leaf. 'banana$' has 7 leaves.

q: Why does a compressed suffix tree have only O(n) nodes, while the suffix trie can have O(n²)?
options: Chains of single-child nodes are merged into one edge, and every internal node has at least two children
It stores only half the suffixes
explain: With n leaves and every internal node branching at least twice, there are at most n − 1 internal nodes.

q: In a suffix tree, where is the longest repeated substring found?
options: At the deepest internal node (by string length)
On the edge from the root with the longest label
explain: An internal node means at least two suffixes share the path to it, so its path string occurs at least twice. For 'banana' it is 'ana'.

q: In the suffix tree of 'banana$', the pattern 'ana' ends at a node with 2 leaves below it, labelled 1 and 3. What does that tell you?
options: 'ana' occurs twice, starting at positions 1 and 3
explain: Each leaf below the end point is a suffix that starts with 'ana', so the leaf labels are the occurrence positions.

q: Which algorithm builds a suffix tree in linear time for a fixed alphabet?
explain: Ukkonen's algorithm is the standard linear-time online construction. Inserting suffixes one by one, as in the page's code, takes O(n²).

q: Every substring of a text T is a prefix of some suffix of T.
explain: True. The substring T[i..j] is the first j − i + 1 characters of the suffix that starts at i. That is the key idea that makes suffix trees work.

q: An N-ary tree has 10 nodes. How many edges does it have?
explain: Every node except the root has exactly one edge to its parent, so any tree with n nodes has n − 1 edges, whatever its branching.
